page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Mutualism is an interaction between two
different species in which BOTH species are
steps.why: One word does all the work here — both — so the definition is short, and the space saved goes into the example where the second mark sits.
common_mistakes: Writing that one is benefited and the other is unaffected. That is commensalism.
Writing about two members of the SAME species. The interaction is between DIFFERENT species.
steps.memory_tip: Mutual means on both sides: in mutualism both partners gain.
steps.margin_note: One sentence only. The word both is the mark.

steps.label: Example
lines: The bee gets nectar and pollen from the
The plant gets pollinated by the bee.
steps.why: Because both partners gain, the example needs two statements of gain — one for each partner — and a student who writes only the bee's gain has shown commensalism, not mutualism.
common_mistakes: Writing only that the bee gets nectar. The plant's gain must be written too.
Giving barnacles and a whale. The whale gains nothing, so that is commensalism.
steps.memory_tip: Bee and flower: nectar goes one way, pollen goes the other. Two gains, two lines.
steps.margin_note: Name the example, then one line of gain for each partner.

insider_note: The mark for the example needs BOTH gains written out — one line for the bee and one for the plant.
